Reflections and inspiration from NEXT Pharma Summit in Dubrovnik…. Congratulations to Dario Safaric and the team for another wonderful event that brought together some of the finest minds in pharma (industry and service side) to share ideas and discuss how we all do things better. This year, I had the pleasure of chairing three debates, alongside the usual catch ups with friends and discussions with clients about my work at VuuAI transforming content engagement. The first panel, ‘Commercial Reloaded: Are We Ready for Today’s & Tomorrow’s HCPs?’ saw Barbara Albientz , David Vanni , and Derek Choy ( Azeeza Sunmonu was greatly missed due to travel difficulties) discuss how we stay relevant to evolving HCP needs. One key conclusion is that we have to explore new channels and ensure we meet the needs of both HCPs and the AI bots serving them information (GEO was a hot topic!). Later, I had the pleasure of diving into the human side of transformation with Lauren Leahy , Alex Condoleon , Laetitia Huret , and Nataliya Andreychuk as we discussed ‘Where Capabilities Count — Rethinking Medical and Commercial Talent for Greater Customer Impact’. While there are, for sure, new ‘hard’ skills required (AI literacy being one of them), there has never been a greater need for essential ‘soft’ skills like adaptability, communication, and resilience. Even old dogs can learn new tricks! Finally, in a debate with friends from Ingemark , we explored ‘From 'No' to 'Now': Building Scalable AI Solutions That IT Processes Can't Slow Down’ – or how to ensure you take IT with you – with Robert Raušel , Iria Gala , Dave Yates , and Thirupathi Pattipaka . Alongside an insightful discussion around thinking beyond the core product about integration, security, and change management, there was a real focus on taking a more ‘AI-centric’ approach to reimagining workflows, rather than just enriching old ones with AI. These summaries barely scratch the surface of incredibly rich discussions and I thank my panellists again for the privilege of sharing the stage with them, and to NEXT for the opportunity. NEXT Pharma Summit is known for providing inspiration around the event from cardboard cut-outs of film characters and the event made me think of one in particular – Rocky Balboa – and his quote: “It ain’t how hard you hit; it’s about how hard you can get hit, and keep moving forward. How much you can take, and keep moving forward. That’s how winning is done.” For sure, we live in challenging times with global macroeconomic uncertainty, rapid change from AI, and constant reorganisations everywhere. I understand that’s unsettling, but the key inspiration from the event for me was the reminder that we can’t sit still – we have to keep innovating. We owe it to the patients we serve. ...more

To counterbalance my last post about how AI is stressing many people out it's nice to also think about the positives, which I touch on in this clip from a great discussion with Stephen Wilson at global healthcare comms agency Amiculum . My advice: lean into the opportunities that AI presents as you learn by using it* and let your mind think about the possibility to reimagine new processes, rather than just making current ones more efficient. We can get to a place where humans win as part of new ways of working that embrace AI. And if those new ways of working also help the right medicines get to the right patients more quickly, then we have an ethical responsibility to drive that forwards. So let's go! 🚀 😎 * within the regulations and your company guidelines / governance, obviously 😉 ...more

Heading to Dubrovnik for NEXT Pharma Summit ? Interested in a free therapy session around the impact of AI on commercial and medical operations in the form of a quick chat onsite? In my role running a startup focussed on AI-powered content optimization I have a lot of conversations with people in the industry and some recurring themes come up, including: - Management wants us to do more with AI but there is no clear direction where - We have lots of pilots going on but none of them seem to scale - I get bombarded by startups all offering the same thing and have no idea which actually work - We don't have the right governance and / or data in place around AI - AI innovation has been centralised and we can't do anything until this group defines their strategy - I don't know whether to build, partner, or buy And this is just the tip of the iceberg for what's on people's minds about AI. So, while I'm in Dubrovnik, I'm interested to meet both current industry friends and new folks to hear your thoughts on the biggest challenges and opportunities for AI for HCP and patient engagement. And if you're not there next week but want a quick coffee call that's also good. All discussion will be confidential and I'm happy to also share my reflections (while AI is a relatively new topic I think there are lessons here from other areas in my 25+ years of working in the industry). I'll then pull consolidated, anonymous perspectives together and share them back. If you're interested just say 'yes' in the comments or feel free to add anything additional in your reply. You can also just grab me onsite (I'll be on stage 3x on day one for those who don't know me). Looking forward to a great event and to sharing ideas to help all of us. See you in Dubrovnik! 😎 Ps. this post was not written using AI 😉 ...more

I always knew I’d make it into the Guinness World Records someday. I just thought it would be for basketball… not DNA. 😂🧬🏀 This week, as part of Genentech Gives Back Week, I joined more than 4,800 colleagues as we reclaimed the world record for the largest human DNA double helix formation. Now I’m debating whether “Guinness World Record holder” belongs in my LinkedIn headline. Jokes aside, this was a special moment. Seeing thousands of colleagues come together around science, community, belonging, and purpose was a powerful reminder of what makes Genentech special. A DNA helix is the perfect symbol for our work: science at the center, powered by people connected around a shared mission. Proud to be part of this moment. Proud to be part of this community. And grateful for everyone who helped make history. For fun: if your colleagues could nominate you for an unofficial world record, what would it be? Mine might be “most likely to make anything a team sport — even a DNA helix.” 😂 Comment 👇🏽 #GenentechGivesBack #Genentech #DNAHelix #Teamwork #CommunityImpact

As many of you already know, I retired last October, though it has taken me some time to write this note. In the months since stepping away from my professional role, my focus shifted to caring for my father, who is living with Alzheimer’s. That transition from work to family naturally slowed my ability to pause and share this milestone, but it has also brought perspective, clarity, and a renewed appreciation for what truly matters. Throughout my career, caring for patients was at the heart of what I did, and it was a privilege I never took lightly. Supporting others during vulnerable moments - listening, advocating, and helping where I could was deeply meaningful work. Today, that role of carer has become more personal as I support my father, giving new depth to the values that shaped my professional life: compassion, patience, and quiet resilience. As I look back, I do so with pride and gratitude. I was fortunate to work alongside remarkable people who made the journey rewarding and memorable. To my colleagues, leaders, teams, advocates and partners: thank you for the trust, collaboration, challenges, and shared successes. I learned so much from working with you all. I step into retirement feeling proud of the work behind me, thankful for the relationships built along the way, and excited for this next chapter. I also want to thank my friends and family for their constant encouragement and support, and especially my partner, Paul, whose love and patience have meant more than words can say. While my days look very different now, I remain connected and I’ll be cheering you on from the sidelines. Thank you for being part of my journey.
